open-source.question: What counts as an open source contribution?
open-source.answer: Any useful, public work that helps a project: code, documentation, tests, issue triage, reviews, reproductions, design, or community support.

open-source.question: How do I find beginner-friendly issues?
open-source.answer: Start with maintainer intent labels like “good first issue” and “documentation”, then filter by recent activity and clear reproduction/acceptance criteria.

open-source.question: What makes a pull request easy to review?
open-source.answer: Small scope, clear summary, links to the issue, and a concrete “how to test” section with commands, logs, or screenshots.

open-source.question: Fork vs branch: which workflow should I use?
open-source.answer: For public repos, fork + PR is the safe default. Branch + PR is common in org repos when you have write access and collaboration needs.

open-source.question: How do I avoid wasting time on stalled projects?
open-source.answer: Check recent commits and PR merges, maintainer responsiveness, and whether CONTRIBUTING docs and issue templates exist before you invest effort.

devops-engineer.question: What does a DevOps engineer do day-to-day?
devops-engineer.answer: Typical work includes CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure automation, reliability practices, observability, incident response, and enabling faster delivery with guardrails.

devops-engineer.question: DevOps vs SRE vs Platform Engineering: what’s the difference?
devops-engineer.answer: DevOps is the collaboration and delivery model; SRE focuses on reliability with error budgets; Platform engineering builds internal platforms to scale delivery across teams.

devops-engineer.question: What skills matter most for DevOps roles in {year}?
devops-engineer.answer: Strong fundamentals (Linux, networking), cloud basics, CI/CD, IaC, containers, and observability. Depth in one area beats shallow familiarity across many tools.

devops-engineer.question: How do I build a DevOps portfolio without production access?
devops-engineer.answer: Ship small but complete demos: IaC + CI + app deploy + monitoring + runbook. Treat “how to operate” as part of the deliverable.

devops-engineer.question: What are common interview pitfalls for DevOps candidates?
devops-engineer.answer: Over-indexing on tool names, not explaining trade-offs, and lacking incident/debugging examples with clear timelines and actions.

product-management.question: What does a product manager actually own?
product-management.answer: PMs own outcomes and decisions: defining the problem, setting priorities, aligning stakeholders, and ensuring teams ship the right thing with measurable impact.

product-management.question: PM vs Product Owner vs Program Manager: how do they differ?
product-management.answer: PM focuses on product outcomes and strategy, PO focuses on backlog execution within agile teams, and program managers coordinate delivery across multiple teams.

product-management.question: How do I write a good PRD?
product-management.answer: Keep it decision-focused: problem, users, constraints, success metrics, scope boundaries, and how to validate. Avoid implementation micromanagement unless needed.

product-management.question: How do I prioritize work with limited data?
product-management.answer: Use lightweight frameworks (RICE, impact/effort), write assumptions explicitly, and run the smallest experiment that reduces uncertainty quickly.

product-management.question: What are common mistakes new PMs make?
product-management.answer: Confusing outputs with outcomes, over-committing scope, skipping alignment, and not defining success metrics before shipping.

unit-testing.question: What is the goal of unit testing?
unit-testing.answer: Unit tests protect behavior at the smallest reasonable scope and make refactoring safer by providing fast, deterministic feedback.

unit-testing.question: Unit vs integration vs end-to-end tests: which should I write?
unit-testing.answer: Start with a small set of high-value integration/E2E tests for critical flows, then add unit tests where logic is complex and changes frequently.

unit-testing.question: What should I avoid mocking?
unit-testing.answer: Avoid mocking your own code heavily. Prefer mocking external boundaries (network, clock, filesystem) and keep assertions behavior-focused.

unit-testing.question: How many tests are “enough”?
unit-testing.answer: Enough tests to catch regressions in core behavior and enable refactors. Coverage is a signal, but stable behavior and fast feedback are the real goal.

unit-testing.question: What are common unit testing mistakes?
unit-testing.answer: Brittle tests coupled to implementation details, slow tests that discourage running locally, and skipping edge cases like timeouts and error handling.

sdlc.question: What is SDLC in simple terms?
sdlc.answer: SDLC is the end-to-end process of building software: planning, design, implementation, testing, release, and maintenance with feedback loops.

sdlc.question: Waterfall vs Agile vs DevOps: which should teams use?
sdlc.answer: Most modern teams use agile delivery plus DevOps practices. Waterfall can work in stable, regulated contexts, but feedback cycles are slower.

sdlc.question: What is the fastest way to improve delivery speed safely?
sdlc.answer: Automate the pipeline, reduce batch size, add tests at the right layer, and use feature flags to decouple deployment from release.

sdlc.question: What metrics should I track for SDLC health?
sdlc.answer: Start with DORA metrics (lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate, MTTR) and add product metrics that reflect outcomes.

sdlc.question: What are common SDLC anti-patterns?
sdlc.answer: Big-bang releases, unclear ownership, manual deployments, and treating quality/security as “after the sprint” instead of part of the workflow.
